x: Ken Miller, John Thresher, Mal Robinson and Bill Kerr are no respecters of reputation and will fight tooth and nail for Belgrave in any race going.
Although Jack beat Mal Robinson and Pat Newell well enough, he was in turn beaten by a guest runner who has since become a familiar figure to most Belgravians - Bill Kerr.
STAGE 9 - Bill Kerr (29.07, 6th fastest). To the uninitiated Belgrave appeared to have gone from the face of the earth at this stage, for the claret and gold vest was nowhere to be seen.

A new face which has been of great help to us this season is that of Scotland's Bill Kerr. An athlete who suffers so little from nerves that either before or after a hard race he can still keep wisecracking, Bill came to us from Victoria Park four months ago, and has already set us a new Club Record in the 2 miles.
He finished 7th in 9:09.0, but Bill Kerr had to retire after 5 laps with a troublesome injury and Robinson and Walker were nowhere near their best.

Most impressive of these was Bill Kerr, whose effort in the 3 miles showed what great potential he possesses. After nearly 2 miles of pace-setting by Stacey (T.V.H.), Bill with Longridge (S.L.H.) broke clear.

Bill Kerr, racing for the first time since his injury, ran a fine 14:14.6 three miles to finish 4th, but the remainder of our team, apart from Peter Eldridge, either failed to qualify for their finals or were outside the first six.
Travelling to his homeland in an endeavour to record times to qualify for the A.A.A. championships, Bill Kerr unwisely ran in the six-mile event on the Friday evening.
John Thresher finished second to international A.J. Harris in the 880, recording a personal best of 1:55.3, and Bill Kerr also did a best ever in the mile, recording 4:13.1 to beat B.C.

Bill Kerr has proved himself a popular character, a fine athlete, and a valuable Club member. He established a new club record of 8:55 for two miles in the London Clubs race, and capped a season of fine running by finishing a good second to T.V.H.

A sensational last-leg stint by Bill Kerr lifted Belgrave into a noteworthy second place, just two secs. ahead of rivals, T.V.H. Amid intense excitement, Bill set off in 4th place 18 secs. behind Herne Hill and a full half minute behind the Valley, and after what must have been the fastest 2 mls. ev…

The whole race was run in a lethargic manner and it was soon obvious that, barring accident, Bill Kerr would be the winner. Jack Brown made a valiant effort to keep the gap as small as possible between himself and the loping Scot ahead, but Bill seemed to have the matter well in hand at all times.
JACK BROWN'S last step for Belgrave before retirement. BILL KERR sets off on Stage nine
Eric Gebbett finished a well placed 8th, Clive Shippen moved up to 6th, Ron Linstead to 4th, and an excellent effort by Bill Kerr took us to 2nd, only 14 secs behind a strong Woodford team.
Although Belgrave were destined for only 5th place in the team result, Bill Kerr enhanced his reputation by clocking fastest time of the day over this 2½ miles cross-country course.
In a 10 - mile paarlauf held at Hurlingham on November 26th, Bill Kerr and Charlie Walker finished second to London University pair, recording 45 mins - 38 secs.
TOP RIGHT: Ron Linstead hands over to Bill Kerr in the Chelmsford Road Relay. BOTTOM LEFT: Belgrave's winning London Brighton Walk team seen passing through Clapham.
BILL KERR
- (by E.D.Lacey) Bill Kerr seen leading an illustrious Portsmouth trio in the Southern.

Bill Kerr and Barry Sawyer have been most unfortunate with injuries and we did not have them both fully fit for any race. Ken Miller has been completely out of training with severe back trouble, Alan Black with a fractured foot, and Charlie Dabbs is still travelling the long road back to fitness.
Bill Kerr and John Davies got away well and after the first half mile were contesting the lead whilst our other runners were all well-placed.
Bill Kerr was our star man. Early on he took up a position in the twenties, and as the race progressed, so did Bill, eventually running home 15th.
BOTTOM LEFT Our winning team in the Mitcham '15' - (left to right) Barry Sawyer, 5th, Bill Kerr, 8th, and Chas.

With an injury-free Bill Kerr to compete also, we can expect a considerable improvement. On this occasion, it is not mere wishful thinking to say they would certainly have enabled us to split Woodford and T.V.H. who finished 6th and 7th.

… years have contested the leading places with considerable vigour and success. 1962 however, was not to be our year for Bill Kerr, Alan Black,Ken Miller and Charlie Dabbs were all on the injured list and we had to call upon reserves who, although putting everything they had into their running, were…

Fireworks were expected when Bill Kerr clung to North like a leech for the first one mile lap; and when Kerr actually overtook the National cross-country champion a ding-dong battle was fully expected.
What happened in between hardly bears relating,for not even a strong following wind could produce good times on any leg except the long stretch beyond Hand Cross which was again taken by Bill Kerr.

Bill Kerr ran a fine(9:25.0)2 miles to beat O'Gorman and Macey of St. Albans, but unfortunately we were short of a runner for the team race one good man could have swung both the Senior and total scores in our favour.

Outstanding Belgrave performer at this evening meeting was Mike Smithers who long jumped 21'5¾" - a mere 9¾" behind U.K. record holder John Howell (H.H.H.) Bill Kerr (9:20:0) was a comfortable winner of the 2 miles but was edged out in the mile by team-mate John Thresher (4:26:4).
In the Southern Counties A.A.A. 6 miles championship at Portsmouth on April 28th, Bill Kerr finished an excellent 5th in 29:19.4, breaking Charlie Dabb's club record by 8.6 seconds.

Our main point-scorers in this match were Gerry Leroy, Bill Kerr, John Thresher and Pat Cornelius. Although beaten in the 220 yards by Marsh of Hercules, Gerry ran a fine 'quarter' to edge out Sunstan (S.L.H.) in 50.9 to show that he is still a force to be reckoned with over one lap.

John Thresher and Bill Kerr fought out the mile with John getting home in 4:13:4 with our Scots laddie following in 4:14:8. Smithers and Leroy had a private battle in the Long Jump with Mike just beating his less experienced rival by the odd half-inch (19'6½" to 19'6").
Don Maclean was 3rd and Bill Kerr 7th. BOTTOM RIGHT: Alan Black who set a new Club Steeplechase record of 9:20.0 in the Scottish Championships.

Secondly, Gerry North was leading the team for the first of what we hope will be many Brighton races and just how well he did it is indicated by his time of 27:27 on the 9th stage, only 2 secs. outside the record set up by Brian Kilby last April and 68 secs. faster than Bill Kerr's Club record.

New faces are always welcome and this season the road running ranks have been swelled by Gerry North, Bill Kerr, Charlie Walker, George Williams John Moore and Peter Wrench; and with Jack Brown showing a return to form, things look good for next season.
Pat, a Scot, was introduced into the Club by Bill Kerr and has already shown useful form. Next season could see him amongst our leading runners.
The foundation was laid on Stage 1 when Bill Kerr came home 5yds down on Harris of Mitcham. John Davies consolidated our second place and John Thresher took us into the lead at the half way mark.

Gerry North and Bill Kerr, therefore, were unable to compete. Walker, Black and Davies got an excellent start and at 3 miles had settled down into 13th, 15th and 17th places with Sawyer in the 20s and Brown in about 30th spot.

These two opened up a lead of 50 yards over Bill Kerr, Laurie O'Hara and Pat Bradley, amongst others. However, Bill then started to get moving and caught the leaders about half a mile from the finish.
Bill Kerr was in great form and set a new course record of 23:29 in beating the Irishman Hogan and Aylesford's Mayatt by 24 secs. and 38 secs. respectively.
John Moore and Derek Crookes were running together a little further back and it was clear we would finish 6 in 40 despite the retirement of John Thresher and Bill Kerr.

We still had fair hopes at the start but the course disposed of them as well and Belgrave were written off in 8th place, for Sawyer had to retire and Bill Kerr's shoe was split by the ice, forcing him to withdraw as well.

Bill Kerr was lying 5th on the last lap when he fell with a badly sprained ankle. Walton again took the team-race, but by a smaller margin from the Bels who scored one point less than in race No.1 but had to go back to 54th place for their 10th scorer.
COVER PHOTO:(by Ed Lacey) Bill Kerr, who gained an A.A.A. vest against Cambridge University where he won the 2 miles event in 9:02.8 after running 10 miles the previous evening.

Bill Kerr finished 7th in the Scottish Championships and was invited to represent his country in the International. I should have thought the opportunity would have been grabbed with both hands, but Bill, no doubt, had good reasons for declining the invitation.
Bill Kerr and Ron Linstead were well down. After the completion of one lap, Gerry had crept up to 14th, Charlie to 85th and Alan Black to 120th.
After a sensational last lap by Bill Kerr, Belgrave were acclaimed winners of this year's promotion from the Gordon Road Drill Hall on March 9th.
Bill Kerr, fresh from his defeat of Hyman in the Ilford, was faced with a similar task but made considerable harder by Hyman having a 20 sec. lead - a somewhat impossible task.

Early pace-setters were Chris Steer and Bill Kerr with Charlie Walker lying handy. At one mile these three led with Cocks and Fairclough, Bradley O'Hara, Dabbs, Angus, Gebbett, Morrison and Maclean following at intervals of a few yards.

Bill Kerr is becoming a regular performer on stage 9 and now knows the ups and downs as well as anyone. To be confronted, however, with a road completely devoid of other runners is not the ideal situation especially as Bill performs at his best when chasing other competitors.

…nd John Thresher to 6th it was left to Gerry North to haul us up to the first four with the day's fastest time (21:11). Bill Kerr set off on the final stage 39 secs behind Manchester D.L.C. (Ward) and 13 secs behind Wallasey (Barlow).…
On the same day Bill Kerr finished 4th in the Middx. 3miles behind Taylor, Briault, and Barratt.
Despite the magnificent running of Gerry and the able support of Kerr and Walker, we didn't figure in the team result as there was a mix-up in the entry and Bill Kerr was unfortunately not nominated.
Bill Kerr, also in the match v. Cambridge U.,won the 2 mls in 9:2.8 just edging out team-mate Tim Briault who had such a fine cross-country season.
Mike Barratt beat Bill Kerr in the two mile but our supporting cast of North (elder) O'Hara, Black and Walker ensured victory in the team contest.

Two other notable track successes were Bill Kerr who won the '6' in 29:42.4 and John Thresher who was 2nd in the 1500 m in 3:50.6 If we had been better represented in the Field Events we would certainly have challenged T.V.H. for the Trophy.
As if by way of compensation for our poor showing in the Field Events Trophy, the Belgrave Team of Geoff North, Bill Kerr and Charlie Dabbs won the 2 mile team race.

Notable senior performers for Belgrave, were Bill Kerr (4:18.2) who won the mile, and Peter Pepe (58.3) who took the 440 hurdles. The home club won the senior match with 100 points to Blackheath's 73 and our 70.

Bill Kerr was way down the field at this stage with Tony Fairclough mistakenly dogging his heels. During the next 3½ laps, Sawyer worked like a Trojan to close the gap and,dropping Newell, eventually passed Laurie just before 2 miles.

The only event for Seniors alone was the 2 miles where Bill Kerr lead from gun to tape in 9:10.2, ahead of Dabbs and Fairclough. Chris Ryan scored a junior sprint double over Turnverein's Rotharmel (10.3 and 23.5) but only managed it by a whisker in the 220 yards.

John Thresher, barely free from injury, was eliminated in his 1 mile heat with 4:10.1, as was Peter Pepe who recorded 56.8 in the 440 yards hurdles. With Bill Kerr (14:00) finishing 12th in the 3 miles we were better represented than for some time.
Taylor (HHH) took the field thro' the first mile in 4:17, but with 2 laps to go Bill Kerr took over and led at the bell, with Tulloh close by and Taylor and Snowden a couple of yards back.

In addition we produced the three fastest individual times of the day thanks to Gerry and Geoff North and Bill Kerr. The 'B' team despite a few weak spots finished sixth and took the first 'B' team awards.

Bill Kerr was in no mood to hang about and bounded straight into the lead which Hyman could do little to reduce. Last time these two met on a final relay stage was at Ilford last March when Bill showed the superior finish.

Bill Kerr, who must by now know the ninth stage quite well also put up the best time of the day and further increased our lead to put us in LEFT:Barry Sawyer looks for the opposition after giving John Thresher an 8 second lead at the first change-over.
A hard tussle ensued but there was little doubt who would come off best and Gerry presented Bill Kerr with a 31 second start for the final leg.
On a flooded, heavy track at Southampton on Sept.4th, and in a constant downpour, Bill Kerr finished off the track season with an excellent 13:57.4 three miles.

Bill Bruce then did a last-leg stint reminiscent of fellow Scot, Bill Kerr; and to everyone's pleasure took two further places with a time faster even than Ron Hayes---which is no mean feat in these "days of Hayes"!

Gerry North was a good winner of this year's promotion from Adcocks (Coventry)and Edwards (Bristol) but despite Bill Kerr and Charlie Dabbs finishing 7th and 8th we were still pipped by Coventry in the team race.
Dabbs was always in sight of the leading group but Bill Kerr was still feeling the effects of his 'Brighton' run the previous week and was not at his best.
Walker in his first run since the 'Brighton' finished a good sixth but Bill Kerr after a hard week's training, gave no indication of how fit he really is.
Without the assistance of Laurie O'Hara and Bill Kerr Cadogan AC still managed 5th place in the Middlesex championships, whilst Belgrave's Surrey team could only manage 7th at Coulsdon.
All of our lads ran to form, apart from Bill Kerr who was currently struggling with a bad patch of form, but Walton won the day yet again and took a winning lead of 81 points.
Although without Kerr and O'Hara, our Middlesex members, running under the name of Cadogan A.C. went two better than their Surrey counterparts by finishing 5th.

These hopes were dented slightly when it was discovered that Charlie Dabbs was still haunted with the injury he sustained just after his great South of Thames run, and Bill Kerr had still not recovered his form, but confidence still ran high.

Bill Kerr showed his old form once again on March 21st when he retaine[illegible] the 'Wimbledon Cup' with the fast time of 27:55. This was particularly pleasing for Bill had been experiencing a patch of bad form for several weeks.

HUGH BARROW sends his regards to all, particularly that "nut-case" fellow scotsman, Bill Kerr. Hugh has been troubled with a persistent leg injury this winter which caused him to miss the Scottish National and a BAAAB trip to LYON for a 2,000 metres indoor race.
With Bill Kerr back to his form to be followed by Gerry North, the result was no longer in dispute and we eventually ran out winners by about 2 mins.

Bill Kerr took the next stage of 5 miles against Lindsell of Portsmouth and Roath of Walton. Although running well enough to beat the previous stage record by 14 seconds, he could make no impression on the Portsmouth runner although closing slightly on Roath.
Bill Kerr was the first to set off down the Prom and ran strongly to bring us in third. Laurie O'Hara closed on the teams in front and Gerry North on the third leg stormed into the lead.
Stage IX - Bill Kerr (28:57 - 11th fastest) Bill has had a miserable winter through a complete loss of form but has recently been back to his usual self.
Our only senior representatives in the A.A.A Indoor Championship at Wembley over Easter were John Thresher and Bill Kerr. Both were eliminated from their heats of the 2 miles event.
…00 metres Steeplechase and clocking 9:24.6 - just 10 yards behind Gibson of Surrey A.C. - and Geoff North (14:44.4) and Bill Kerr (14:48.8) chasing Alan Perkins home in the 5000 metres.…

A flat out first lap by Bill Kerr and Dave Baines broke up the senior mile field straight away but Geoff North and Tony Fairclough had to run the next three laps in their respective lonesome positions of 1st and 2nd.

The main reason for Langen's victory was their domination of the field events,but we swept the board in the middle distance races with fine wins by John Thresher and Jim Hogan who were well supported by Bill Kerr,Tony Fairclough and Chas.

This presented Bill Kerr with the unenviable task of giving John Cooke a 13 second lead and a beating - a feat even North couldn't have managed, for Cooke's time was second fastest of the day, only one second down on Gerry.

Unfortunately Gerry was not at his absolute best and instead of picking up Hyman as we had hoped,he was forced to drop back ten seconds leaving Bill Kerr the invidious task of chasing the other and better of the Cooke boys.

Bill Kerr showed a welcome return to form when he took the Autumn "trial" in convincing style from Fairclough and Dabbs. Several of our leading runners were not taking part and it was apparent that any potential "Brighton" man would have to make the first eight to be worthy of further consideration.

In good conditions Bill Kerr ran a fine race to win this long '5' (appx. 5 miles 1100yds)by 17 secs from John Pettitt. Jack Brown and Mike Shingles also ran well to finish 7th and 10th respectively,but we still only managed 2nd team behind Maidstone who packed 3,4 and 5.

Bill Kerr also ran well to finish 18th and Trevor Hart must have had one of his best races ever to finish 25th in what,to all intents and purposes,is an unofficial road race Championship of the South of England.
In Scotland he is first claim Victoria Park AAC, which is Bill Kerr's home club. Hugh is a dedicated runner from whom great things can be expected.
After 2 miles Geoff North, Fairclough, Thorpe, Black, Dabbs and O'Hara were closely bunched with Black and Geoff North setting the pace; Bill Kerr was already finding their speed too fast.

We fielded four teams and would surely have won the team race if one more of our better runners had been able to turn out. As it was,Don Maclean was called upon to back up Bill Kerr and Laurie O'Hara. We were only beaten by one point for third team place.

At the first bend Gerry North was knocked over and Bill Kerr badly baulked. However, fine packing gave BELGRAVE the team race, our four scorers being 3rd Kerr 9:12, 4th O'Hara 9:15, 6th Gerry North 9:20, 8th Hart 9:29.

Disaster struck for Bill Kerr at the Crystal Palace evening meeting on August 17th. Whilst attempting to vault a wall just before the start of the 2 miles he slipped, fell and gashed his leg sufficiently badly to go to hospital for stitching.
Bill Kerr tried to continue the good work but, for him, his run was not spectacular. John Dear passed Mitcham on stage 8 but had to allow Poly to pass.
Could Bill Kerr keep close enough to Kilby and Bullivant to give our last three runners a chance or would these top class runners open up a large gap?

Mel Thorpe (in great form these days) was second in 4:19.8 and Bill Kerr third in 4:20.2. The 3000m Steeplechase (a new championship event which should become more popular) proved an easy victory for John Bicourt whose experience at this type of race was too much for John Dear who had led in the early stages .

Bill Kerr and John Thresher both recorded personal bests,but,dare I mention it,the honours must go to Geoff North who was only narrowly beaten by our old friend Jim Hogan,reducing the Club Record somewhat into the bargain.

Bill Kerr ran well in the 'A' mile,both he and Herring (Blackheath) closing on the leader in the last lap. Even with his final 'kick' Laurie O'Hara still couldn't catch Huffer (TVH) in the 'B' event,but once again he triumphed over his Blackheath rival John Baldwin.
Charlie Walker and Bill Kerr did their 'old pal's act' and finished equal 7th. Arthur Bruce had a good run to complete our scoring team.
Bill Kerr showed he is gradually returning to form with an encouraging 24th place. He should strike form just right for the County, Area and National Championships.

The remainder of our team had by this time appeared and with Bill Kerr and Laurie O'Hara closing in with our fastest times and narrowing the gaps ahead we finished a good 3rd behind very strong Ealing and Essex Beagles teams.
Our 'B' team were 5th, and with Bill Kerr doing a great 17:46 "come back" and Bill Dance anchoring in 17:55 we had two men faster than Major and Steer in the 'A' team

It was good to see Bill Kerr out of hibernation to run a sound 5000m. Our only win of the afternoon came when Ray Middleton thrashed the opposition in the 2 mile walk for a meeting record time of 14:47.2 .

What good news it is that Bill Kerr is running into form again. After showing tremendous promise in his early days with us - he was our No.1 before Gerry North arrived on the scene - he has since had his ups and downs and many thought we had seen the last of him.
This provided a real test for Bill Kerr, who has just got back to fitness after a long lay off, but he displayed quite a large slice of his old form and had little difficulty in holding our lead.
(Photo by Stanley Devon) The ruck of the G.L.C. field splash past the mile mark at Parliament Hill, with John Dear (16) and Bill Kerr (17) in the thick of it.
Laurie O'Hara was very unhappy with the going and his 20th position, although creditable, belied his true form. John Dear finished 36th and Bill Kerr 41st, but Cadogan could not close in a team.

RIGHT: Bill Kerr paces "World Sports" star Charlie Walker! Bill Dance had his first outing since a bout of achilles trouble and performed surprisingly well, but Bicourt, Steer (retired) and Kerr disappointed.

Bill Dance had not yet recovered from his fast start and was already in the sights of Bill Kerr in the eighties. Brian Buxton looked quite distressed and it was unfortunate that our "twelve cup" chances should disappear with his withdrawal early in the second lap.
Bill Kerr, still on the come-back trail, ran steadily through the field, no doubt under strict orders from his adviser - Charlie Walker !! - who finished just behind him.
Once again Charlie Walker and Bill Kerr did their 'old pals act' with Arthur Bruce making a determined but unsuccessful effort to split them towards the end.

At the mile post we had 3 in 70, with the remainder outside 120 and Bill Kerr trailing around the 200 mark. The positions after one lap are not usually far off the final score and at this point we had North 8, Thresher 35, Fairclough 58, Hart 97, Williams 119, Bicourt 130, Dance 150, O'Hara 154 and Kerr 160.
Bill Kerr, fast regaining his form of old, made a lot of ground in the final stages, but John Thresher once again showed his dislike for road races in excess of 4 miles.

Slowest of our ten runners was Bill Kerr whose time was beaten last year by only Gerry North and Laurie O'Hara. This time it was Bill Dance's turn for relegation to the 'B' team and he gave the only sensible answer to such decisions - a time faster than two of our 'A' men!

Spirits sank when Gerry Williams' pre-race "test" confirmed his withdrawal from the team, but rose again when it was understood Gerry North would be taking a long stage after all. The only other change was Bill Kerr to replace Bill Dance on a long stage. STAGE 1: Geoff North (28:45 - 14th fastest)

At about half-way 'Flying Scotsman' Kerr ran out of steam and was picked up by the main pack at an alarming rate. Now Alan Black started to drop, though not so quickly, and Tony Fairclough seemed to have the race all sewn up.
If Peter Whewell is still with us in early October and Bill Kerr and Adrian Major can keep free of injury then our depth should carry us through to some big wins.
At Woking on September 9th Bill Kerr got our non-scoring 'B' team off to a good start in the County relay championship when he finished 2nd.

Chris Steer and Bill Kerr, the only other two ever in the hunt, were dropped on the return journey but once over their bad spell hugn on tenaciously to close in the half-dozen well over a minute ahead of the remainder.
Bill Kerr loped away in his usual relaxed style and although not setting the course on fire brought us up to 4th by dealing severely with the Ealing runner.
RIGHT:An angelic Bill Kerr takes over from a top form Gerry Williams. STAGE 6: Adrian Major (16:04 - 3rd fastest)

Bill Kerr on the penultimate leg with the fastest time of the day on this stage made the situation even more exciting and pulled up closely to Leicester Colleges - a really first class performance out of the Bill Kerr mould.

Despite the central venue, though, and one of our best turn-outs we were still without Trevor Hart, Bill Kerr and Pat Newell. Our best team would probably have taken 4th place, instead, we were 10th and last.
Including our reserve (Dabbs), five of our thirteen runners are over 30 years of age---headed by Bill Kerr, 36 next month. On June 1st the average age of the team was 28 years-4 months.
Things were now hotting up and at the bottom of Copse, Hart, O'Hara, Bicourt and Major had broken away from Bill Dance with Bill Kerr and John Dear close up and the rest strung out in single file.

Bill Kerr (14:38 - 2nd fastest) Bill was his usual unruffled self at the takeover and, as he left the stadium in that misleadingly nonchalant style, many thought that Taylor of Derby would consolidate their lead.
He admires Gerry North immensely for his wholehearted approach and has a high regard for Bill Kerr - "A beautifully relaxed performer whom I tried to copy".
Bill Kerr's decision to run at almost the eleventh hour meant he was not in our team entry and hence not able to score, thus making Lionel Mann with another good run our third scoring member.
On paper it looks like John Thresher, but look out for Bill Kerr who has improved tremendously over the mile. Also Geoff North who if encouraged enough could give both of these a run for their money.
Howard Satchell in the pole position and John Bicourt quickly go into the lead followed up by Adrian Major and John Thresher ... in the back straight Bill Kerr quickly overtakes the early leaders ...
Bill Kerr towed the mile field through the first three laps and Thresher was the only one with him at the bell. Bill was in his most stylish form and looks well set for some good 3's this season.
As the 3-milers recuperated, it was announced that the first 10 had run faster than the winner of their rival County, Middlesex; the winner being none other than our own Bill Kerr.

Bill Kerr won the three miles in 14:04.2 with Laurie O'Hara third in 14:12.0. Our second claim long jumper Alan Lerwill took his speciality with a leap of 22'-8¾", but John Dear had an unhappy outing in the steeplechase with his season's slowest of 10:04---neverless he still got a bronze for his effort!
The heat was oppressive and Bill Kerr, running at the worst time of all, showed magnificent fighting qualities in the 5000 metres. He finished 4th in 14:36.2, 14.2 seconds behind P.
Adrian Major, 3rd in the mile, Bill Kerr and Gerry North, 2nd and 3rd in the 'three', and Bill Dance 2nd in the 'chase' were the highlights of Belgrave's 2nd placing behind T.V.H. - by just 3 points.

This defeat can mainly be blamed on Hillingdon's Andy Kerr who trains with Bels. Full marks to Chris Martin who scored a double in the sprints, Adrian Major for a personal best mile and Bill Kerr in the three miles.

On an undulating track, Adrian Major equalled his best mile ever, whilst Gerry North and Bill Kerr both returned good two-mile times. In the sprints, Jim Vivian looked more like his old self and John Mitchell powered round to an easy 220 yards win.

Scoring a double win in the 100 yards, Jim Vivian 9.8 and John Mitchell 10.0, Belgrave were also first in the 3000 metres steeplechase, Dick Pitrowski 9:1.4, the 'B' Mile, Bill Kerr 4.15.4 and the 'B' 220, Jim Vivian 22.2.

Bill Kerr and Gerry North were a little disappointing in the 5,000 and 10,000 respectively. Throughout the afternoon we had been alternately well in the lead and fractionally in front with Blackheath pushing us closely.

Bill Kerr took the field through the early stages at a brisk pace with Fairclough, O'Hara, Mann and Pitrowski in close attendance. At 4 miles Fairclough was back in his usual role of pacemaker with his shadow, O'Hara (mud-spattered from top to toe) close alongside.
Gerry North, John Thresher, Laurie O'Hara, Adrian Major, Tony Fairclough, John Bicourt, Dick Piotrowski, Bill Dance, Bill Kerr, Trevor Hart, John Dear, Lionel Mann, Roger Donnison

Such names as Adrian Major, Bill Kerr, Chris Martin, 'Snowy' Brooks and Phillip Gee. These fellows were always prepared to turn up to any meeting in any conditions and without them Bels would certainly not have fared as well as they did.
Not far behind, in one of his best ever road runs was John Dear a full minute clear of Kelly Diprose and Bill Kerr---both only recently back in training again.
North Surrey League - and Bill Kerr's "The Bridges".

Bill Kerr was recently awarded the 'Charlie Davies' bowl as the G.P.O. South Centre Area's sporting personality of the year for his performance in winning the Middlesex County 3 miles track championship of 1968.

STAGE 4: Bill Kerr (16:07---5th fastest) Bill loped off in his usual relaxed style and soon caught and passed Walton's Doggett, but Bell of TVH opened up an extra 25 seconds on Bill to give his club a useful lead of 36 seconds.

Bill Kerr, the veteran (well almost) kept us in fifth place and narrowed the gap by thirteen seconds - a good performance. Geoff North, now running into form took Stage 5 and with a time of 27:24.0 produced our best long stage time of the day.

Last year's individual winner Laurie O'Hara was not so fit this time and was chased home by Bill Kerr to complete our 'A' team. As usual in this race, and as indicated by the results, many personal duels were fought and we hope justice was done; but the 1 sec. difference between Brian Gorman and Bob…

I'm worried about Jim - Rimmer that is - Three false starts in a non scoring 800 m at Battersea and he claimed Tony Brooks pushed him ... then the pistol failed to fire. - As Bill (MAN IN A SUITCASE) Kerr said, "the start was better than the race".
Our best performers in this event were all basically under-distance in John Thresher, Geoff North, Adrian Major and Bill Kerr, well though they performed.

In addition, new stage records were set by Bill Kerr, Gerry North and Peter Morris. The short season was rounded off with what should have been it's major event---the inaugural 6-stage National Relay at the Crystal Palace.

Rumour has it that the whole team was almost put in jeopardy when, in the early hours of the morning before leaving London, Pat O'Connor and Bill Kerr went searching for Lionel Mann inside the grounds of Buckingham Palace---sounds like another of these "An Englishman, an Irishman and a Scotsman tales"!!.

Stage 2.- In spite of Bill Kerr promising to close the gap it was not to be one of his good runs and although we retained our third position Stoke had increased their lead from 9 to 22s with MDLC second and Blackheath close on our heels some 3secs behind.

Bill Kerr supported well as non-scoring runner in twentieth place thus making a very exciting team race. Charlie Walker (44th) led the Belgrave Vets to second place in the Veterans section aided by Arthur Bruce and Bill Matthews.
PREMISES TO SHARE - Well known kilt designer and Haggis stitcher, Bill Kerr, want to sub-let the other half of his suitcase to partner with similar interest.

Alan Black showed a welcome return to form in 5th place and Dave Trow again beat the handicapper, despite having his 10:00 mark in the '7' cut to 7:00 for the longer race. Bill Kerr missed the opportunity of making the Southern "twelve" with an indifferent run, even allowing for a momentary diversion.
Bill Kerr and Charlie Walker dropped a further place each on stage 4 so at the half-way mark we were 5th (4:17 in arrears) and 12th (first 'B' team 9 seconds ahead of H/W).
Bill Kerr and Lionel Mann were in the former category (after good runs in the National) and we were well beaten by Medway in the most minor race of all.

This stage saw a 5 second improvement in our position, but Medway had displaced Reading, so Dick's run had brought us almost to the lead which was well and truly established on the next stage by Bill Kerr who led the way to the tune of 32 seconds - our strength in depth was beginning to show.

Making one of his rare appearances in the distance events it was Bill Kerr who, by virtue of his 19th position, just clinched the second team position for us in front of Medway A.C. thus improving on our last year's position of third.
Other promising runs have come from Peter Carton, Bill Curtin, Bill Kerr, Adrian Major, Bob Smith and Jim Rimmer. This could be one of our stronger events.
With John Bicourt(3rd), Trevor Hart (5th) and Bill Kerr(10th) in this race,we were very well represented. Altogether the Championships were a fine affair.

LEFT: Bill Kerr leads Guy Monnet (116) and John Thresher, the winner, on the second lap of the Senior 1500 metres. RIGHT:Bob Coates on his way to an impressive win over Wil Wesch in the 10,000 metres walk.
Bill Kerr, for some unknown reason, stopped at half way and resumed some way down the field. Peter lost contact during the second half of the race but held his position very well.

Other useful performances came from Steve White, Peter Carton, John Boardman, Adrian Major, Bill Kerr, Lee Sullivan and Glyn Ratcliffe. One can say that it was a good team effort, but just wait and see what we can do at Wimbledon Park!

BILL KERR (66) on his way to a personal best 3:53.4 1500 metres at the age of 38. JOHN THRESHER (6), a youngster of 30(!), was one fifth of a second behind, in this Southern League Meeting at Wimbledon Park.

Here comes the Surrey League field, with Lionel Mann and Bill Kerr at the front.

Bill Kerr was not at his best, however, on the third leg, falling to 16th, with a time of 27m. 58s. Peter Carton, just turned 18, came into the team, and gave a hint of things to come, returning 15m. 43s. to pick up one place.
Fourth leg: Bill Kerr pulled us back up to 13th, but can't have been very pleased with his time of 16m. 16s.

1500m It seems we have no problem here with JOHN THRESHER and evergreen BILL KERR (a Vet next year by the way) our main contenders. Others aiming to get into the team will be PETER CARTON, BILL CURTIN, JOHN STOW, JOHN BICOURT, LAURIE O'HARA and JIM RIMMER, who says he's fitter than ever("I'am doing…

Jim Rimmer confirmed his new "star" rating, by winning the 800m., and Bill Kerr won a surrealist steeplechase. Willie Williams was a hat-trick man in the junior events, while old rivals and team-mates John Stow and Bill Curtin shared the 800m. and 1,500m. titles, with John taking the former, and Bill the latter.
Steve White chalked up yet another sprint double, and Bill Kerr took the 1500m., while Jim Rimmer (3rd in 1m. 57.5s.) and John Boardman (fourth in 1m. 58s.) can be said to have run well in the 800m.

Tony Fairclough and Bill Kerr now live within about six miles of each other in the Gillingham/Sittingbourne area. Nearby, of course, is Geoff North who was actually seen watching a race recently - though it was difficult to tell whether it had any effect on him!
At the Barnet Sports Gala Meeting Laurie O'Hara won the 3000m in 8:36 with Bill Kerr 3rd in 9:04, Clive Shippen 4th in 9:13 and Pat Newell 6th in 9:17.

With Tony Fairclough suffering from a heavy cold and joining the supporters, it was left to a still far from fit Bill Kerr, straight from a decorating session at home and still with paint in his hair, to complete our scoring team.
Bill Kerr showed that Laurie O'Hara is not the only speedy veteran around with his 4:06 timing in the 1500m and Leo Coy improved his steeplechase again, getting closer to 10 minutes.
Bill Kerr ran 8:47 and right into the reckoning for subsequent team selection, beating Colin Pearson into the bargain. Colin nevertheless set his best ever time with 8:51.
Bill Kerr improved our best to 4:31 on leg 50 and was almost immediately overtaken by John Stow who remained far and away our fastest until John Bicourt's 98th leg of 4:14.
Laurie O'Hara and Bill Kerr, our dependable veteran duo, again did their stuff in the 1500m and Arnold Bentt, back after an illness, proved yet again that lack of training means nothing to him.
The Autumn '5¾' road race. Top left: John Davis, Paul Pringle and Bill Kerr
Walker was 42nd and Bill Kerr 60th of the 125 starters.
Callum sneaked yet another prize to add to his Boxing Day booty and third in the handicap was Alan Mead who had a run out of the blue and even had the audacity to overtake Bill Kerr on lap three.

Bill Kerr on only 2 weeks training led on the first leg, but faded in the finishing straight to hand over to Bill Laws in 4th place. Bill ran steady laps of 66 and 65 to pass to Mitcham runner and Keith Sinclair held this position to the final handover.

Bill Kerr, also now in his late 40's, showed a very impressive improvement. However, it is strange to note that our vets remain peculiarly disorganised and one sometimes despairs of them developing a proper racing programme with in-depth support for our top men.
The Junior record was taken to a fast 28.01 by Tony Fairclough in March 1964 behind one of Bill Kerr's four wins while 1965 saw the first of Laurie O'Hara's record six wins (four in the March race).
Including our reserve (Dabbs) five of our thirteen runners are over 30 years of age, headed by Bill Kerr, 36. The average age of the team is 28yrs 4mths.
This performance put Colin into the 12-stage team ahead of Bill Kerr, much to the astonishment of Charlie Walker and the more established runners.
